How it works

Three steps, one long weekend sorted.

No forms, no fifty browser tabs of blog posts. Just a conversation that turns into a plan you can actually book.

01

Tell Yaadgar

Chat naturally — where, when, who's coming, and roughly what you want to spend. Roman-Urdu, Urdu, or English, all fine.

EN"4 days in Hunza, budget 60k for two"
Roman"4 din Hunza jana hai, budget 60k, 2 log"
اردو"حنزہ میں 4 دن، بجٹ 60 ہزار، دو افراد"
02

Get a real itinerary

An AI itinerary engine checks it against actual Pakistani hotels, guides and transport — never invented listings.

Book and go

Why Yaadgar

Your trip has a hundred small decisions. We made the annoying ones disappear.

Every travel app says "personalized." Inside Pakistan, that word has to survive washed-out roads, closed passes, and hotels that don't answer their phone. Here's what it actually means.

①

Never a hotel that ghosts you

Every listing Yaadgar suggests has been checked, in person, before it ever reaches your itinerary — the price is the price, the room is the room.

Growing weekly — stays, guides and rides added across the north, south and cities
✓ Riverside guesthouse, Karimabad — visited & verified
✓ Private 4×4 with driver, Karimabad — verified
✓ Eagle's Nest viewpoint — route confirmed
②

Down to the last rupee

Set a number and watch the whole trip bend around it. Swap a hotel, drop a day, add a car — the total updates before you finish clicking.

③

A co-pilot once you're on the road

Weather, closures, and one tap to your driver — because the plan doesn't stop mattering when the trip starts.

Babusar Pass expected to close early afternoon — plan your crossing before 1pm.
Light snow expected in Naran tonight — an extra layer is worth packing.
④

It knows Hunza isn't Murree

Permits, passes, and the season each valley actually wants — built in from the start, not bolted on after.

Khunjerab Pass — open May to November, permit included in your plan.
